strengths: Novel representation-space perspective on machine unlearning that is well-motivated and addresses real scalability limitations of parameter-centric approaches
Rigorous mathematical framework with systematic derivation of variational bounds and detailed proofs in appendices
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, unlearning scenarios, and baselines with both accuracy and efficiency metrics
Significant practical computational advantages: 143-754x speedups and 2-4x lower memory compared to best baselines, enabling large-scale deployment
Dual-regime design addressing both standard and zero-shot settings, with creative use of Neural Collapse for proxy target generation in privacy-constrained scenarios
Excellent mechanistic insight via 2D toy example visualizing the unlearning process without dimensionality reduction artifacts
Detailed ablation studies examining sensitivity to hyperparameters and architecture choices with comprehensive sensitivity heatmaps
Strong performance on complex datasets (CIFAR-100, Tiny ImageNet) where parameter-based methods degrade significantly
weaknesses: Critical unjustified assumptions: (1) Gaussian modeling of encoder output with identity variance lacks empirical validation; (2) Neural Collapse assumption only holds in terminal training phases; (3) no analysis of what happens when assumptions are violated

Significant hyperparameter sensitivity with dataset-dependent optimal beta values; utility collapse occurs at high beta on complex datasets (e.g., 1% accuracy with beta=10^-1 on Tiny ImageNet); no principled selection method provided

Incomplete privacy analysis: no formal privacy guarantees or certified unlearning; membership inference attacks as sole privacy metric are insufficient and potentially confounded by utility preservation; missing evaluation of other attack vectors

Limited novelty in individual components primarily combines existing ideas (variational MI bounds from Alemi et al. 2016, information bottleneck from Tishby et al. 2000, Neural Collapse from Papyan et al. 2020); contribution is mainly in application rather than methodological innovation

Unjustified design choices: why specifically penultimate layer for Z with no ablation on layer selection; Linear Representation Hypothesis contradicted by ablations showing deeper networks outperform linear ones; no sensitivity analysis on representation dimension

Zero-shot setting requires per-class counts still limiting true data-freeness; Figure 3(c) shows increased retain cluster distortion without real data anchoring; no robustness analysis for incorrect or unavailable class counts
Marginal accuracy improvements in some cases (CIFAR-10 class unlearning where SISA achieves better forget accuracy); primary advantage is computational efficiency rather than unlearning quality

Limited experimental scope restricted to image classification with no evaluation on language models or other domains where unlearning is increasingly critical; missing comparisons to recent baselines like LoRA-based unlearning
Successive relaxation of variational bounds with no analysis of cumulative tightness loss; feasibility and practical implications of the bound approximations remain unvalidated

Inadequate treatment of privacy and ethics given paper topic; impact statement dismisses societal implications despite unlearning being core to privacy regulation compliance and potential misuse concerns

strengths: Clear problem formulation with information-theoretic justification for representation-space unlearning; the approach is intuitive and well-motivated
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets and scenarios (class/random unlearning, standard/zero-shot settings); extensive ablations and sensitivity analyses in appendices
Strong empirical results showing superior forget accuracy, utility retention, and computational efficiency (up to 754× speedup); demonstrates scalability advantages of the approach
Addresses both practical setting (retain data available) and challenging zero-shot scenario; provides explicit algorithms with detailed pseudocode
Good presentation with helpful visualizations (2D mechanistic insight, Figure 3); substantial appendices with hyperparameter details supporting reproducibility
weaknesses: Limited technical novelty: representation-space operation is a straightforward idea; variational bounds use standard techniques (Alemi et al. 2016, Poole et al. 2019) without new theoretical insights

Critical unvalidated assumptions undermine soundness: Neural Collapse hypothesis is essential for zero-shot method but never empirically verified on tested datasets/architectures; Linear Representation Hypothesis and Gaussian parameterization assumed without justification; no analysis of bound tightness

Serious experimental methodology issues: error bars are predominantly ±0 suggesting single runs with questionable statistical validity; baseline methods achieve suspiciously poor performance (EMMN: 1.2% accuracy), raising fairness concerns; no error analysis or significance testing

Misleading terminology and design choices: 'zero-shot' setting still requires forget data access, class counts, and classifier weights—not zero-shot by standard definitions; reference batch construction in Eq. 17 samples from data containing forget examples, creating potential information leakage

Severely limited experimental scope: restricted to three small image classification datasets and ResNet-only architectures; no evaluation on NLP, graphs, other domains, or modern architectures; generaliz­ability claims unsupported

Loose theoretical bounds with multiple approximation layers (Eqs. 2→5, 12→15→16→17) may result in poor surrogates; no analysis of when approximations fail; lack of formal privacy guarantees (e.g., differential privacy)

Weak evaluation metrics: forget accuracy (Af) is indirect privacy measure; only considers MIA attacks (relatively weak); test CE is indirect utility proxy; missing stronger privacy attacks (model inversion, attribute inference)

Unjustified hyperparameter choices: fixed β=10^-3 despite sensitivity analysis showing data-dependent optimal values (Figure 5); identity initialization not motivated; incomplete justification for architectural constraints on fϕ

strengths: Novel representation-centric perspective on machine unlearning, shifting from high-dimensional parameter space to lower-dimensional representation space—a well-motivated and technically sound approach
Solid information-theoretic framework with principled variational bounds deriving tractable surrogates (Equations 2, 6, 12, 16, 19) from intractable mutual information objectives
Addresses both practical scenarios: standard setting (with retain data) and zero-shot setting (without retain data), the latter using creative Neural Collapse-based approximations

Exceptional computational efficiency gains (up to 754× speedup on Tiny ImageNet) and significantly lower memory footprint (2-3× reduction) compared to all baselines—practically valuable for deployment

Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, architectures, and baselines, with detailed ablation studies (Appendix F) examining sensitivity to hyperparameters and architecture depth
Strong reproducibility: complete pseudocode (Appendix B), comprehensive hyperparameter specifications (Appendix D), detailed mathematical derivations (Appendix A), and code availability statement
Clear mechanistic insights via 2D visualization (Figure 3) showing controlled collapse of forget clusters while preserving retain geometry without dimensionality reduction artifacts
weaknesses: Variational bounds are applied sequentially (Eq. 2 → Eq. 5, Eq. 16 → Eq. 17), accumulating approximation error with no empirical analysis of tightness or quantification of information loss; unclear whether minimizing empirical losses achieves the original information-theoretic objectives

Neural Collapse assumption (Eq. 8: p_θ(z|y=c) ≈ δ(z - w_c)) critical for zero-shot method but never empirically validated in the paper; applicability to imbalanced datasets, early training phases, or architectures without Neural Collapse is unexplored

Significant performance degradation in zero-shot setting on complex datasets: Tiny ImageNet zero-shot achieves only 51.6% retain accuracy vs. 59.7% for Retraining; these failures are acknowledged but not deeply analyzed

Hyperparameter sensitivity without principled selection: β = 10^-3 fixed uniformly across experiments, yet ablations show sharp 'utility collapse' at high β with optimal values varying significantly by dataset; no guidance for practitioners to select β without access to retain data

Limited experimental scope: only vision classification (CIFAR-10/100, Tiny ImageNet) with ResNet/WideResNet architectures; applicability to Transformers, LLMs, or non-vision domains unclear; scalability claims based on relatively small models

Several zero-shot baselines show catastrophic failures (EMMN: 1.2% retain accuracy, Table 1; GKT: 45.5% on Tiny ImageNet), making it unclear whether poor performance reflects implementation issues or fundamental limitations; no comparison with simple representation-level baselines (e.g., Gaussian noise replacement)
Lack of formal privacy guarantees: information-theoretic objective does not formally imply unlearning, and MIA is only a heuristic proxy; no differential privacy or certified privacy bounds provided
Gaussian parameterization (Eq. 3-4) simplifies KL divergence to squared Euclidean distance, a strong assumption; no empirical validation that representations follow isotropic Gaussians

strengths: Substantial computational efficiency: Achieves up to 757× speedup over retraining with minimal GPU memory overhead (1.9 GB vs. 8.3-9.8 GB for baselines), making this a practically significant contribution

Comprehensive experimental evaluation: Two unlearning protocols, multiple datasets, 5 random seeds, extensive ablations (Appendices F-G), hyperparameter sensitivity analysis, and GPU profiling demonstrate thorough empirical rigor

Technically sound framework: Variational bounds are correctly derived; application of information-theoretic techniques is mathematically rigorous with proper use of Jensen's inequality and KL divergence manipulations

Addresses both standard and zero-shot settings: The dual-regime approach is valuable for practical scenarios where retain data access is restricted. Creative use of Neural Collapse for zero-shot unlearning
Well-motivated and timely problem: Machine unlearning is important (GDPR/CCPA), and representation-level approach sensibly addresses scalability bottlenecks of parameter-centric methods
Strong reproducibility: Detailed hyperparameters for all baselines, promised code release, and comprehensive appendices support reproducibility
weaknesses: Critical black-box threat model limitation: Method only works for API-access scenarios. Raw representation Z still encodes forget set information, making it vulnerable to white-box attacks. This significantly restricts practical applicability but is under-emphasized in main text

Heavy reliance on Neural Collapse hypothesis for zero-shot: Graceful degradation analysis (Appendix G.2) shows accuracy drops from 93.2% to 71.5% with noise σ=0.3. Table 12 shows weaker collapse on Tiny ImageNet (NC4=0.9355), creating dataset-dependent performance bounds

Circular reference batch concern in forget loss (Eq. 17): Reference batch contains forget data and model hasn't been updated, so aggregate statistics still encode forget information. Theoretical justification for why this removes information is unclear

Questionable privacy metrics: Random unlearning RMIA scores show Rep. Unl. slightly above Retraining baseline (e.g., CIFAR-100: 70.9 vs 68.7), suggesting comparable or less effective privacy. Class unlearning forget accuracy is indirect proxy for memorization removal

Limited technical novelty: Applies established variational information-theoretic bounds (Alemi et al. 2016, Poole et al. 2019) to representation space. Main contribution is application domain rather than algorithmic innovation

Limited scope and generalization: Only image classification tested (CIFAR-10/100, Tiny ImageNet). No evaluation on NLP, LLMs, or other domains. Only ResNet architectures tested. Severely limits claims about general applicability

Significant hyperparameter sensitivity on complex datasets: Method shows brittleness in zero-shot regime. Different optimal β values across settings. Random unlearning is 'significantly more sensitive' to β than class unlearning
Baseline implementation concerns: EMMN achieves only 23.3% on CIFAR-10 (surprisingly poor), making comparisons less interpretable. Some baselines may be inadequately tuned

strengths: Significant computational efficiency gains (100-750× speedups) with minimal memory overhead, addressing practical deployment concerns
Principled information-theoretic formulation grounded in mutual information minimization, more conceptually rigorous than parameter-centric heuristics
Addresses both standard and zero-shot unlearning scenarios, handling realistic constraints on data access
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple datasets, unlearning scenarios, and detailed hyperparameter ablations with honest limitation discussion
Clear algorithmic presentation with reproducibility details (hyperparameters, pseudocode) and promised code release
weaknesses: Fundamental threat model limitation inadequately highlighted: method operates only under black-box assumption with unchanged encoder parameters, leaving raw representations vulnerable to white-box attacks—this is a critical constraint not prominent in abstract/introduction

Significant disconnect between elegant MI formulation and actual objectives: variational bounds, Gaussian assumptions, and Jensen's inequality reduce to simple MSE consistency losses without analysis of tightness or justification of approximation choices

Heavy dependence on Neural Collapse hypothesis for zero-shot variant, which: (1) doesn't universally hold (degrades on Tiny ImageNet with NC4=0.9355), (2) creates rigid utility ceiling, (3) shows graceful degradation claims are overstated (utility drops from 93.2% to 71.5% with moderate proxy noise)

Privacy evaluation concerns: RMIA results show method achieves worse privacy than retraining baseline on both CIFAR-10 (57.7% vs 54.2%) and Tiny ImageNet (75.6% vs 73.0%), contradicting core claims; only weak RMIA metric tested, no gradient-based attacks or model inversion evaluated

Hyperparameter robustness issues: inconsistent optimal β across datasets, random unlearning requires extremely conservative β≤10⁻³ to avoid utility collapse, suggests poor objective calibration and need for per-task tuning

Experimental concerns: some baselines appear poorly tuned (EMMN 1.2% accuracy on CIFAR-100), zero-shot utility gaps are substantial (51.6% vs 58.7% on Tiny), limited evaluation to image classification only, no modern architecture testing (Vision Transformers), missing empirical comparison with concept erasure methods
Technical gaps: no convergence analysis for Algorithm 1, Gaussian distributional assumption not ablated, bound tightness not analyzed, class prior estimation from small forget sets not addressed
Insufficient ethical discussion: Impact Statement dismisses concerns inappropriately given unlearning's potential for misuse

strengths: Novel representation-space approach to unlearning that is well-motivated: representation spaces are orders of magnitude smaller than parameter spaces, making the learning problem more tractable
Solid information-theoretic foundation with properly derived variational upper bounds for intractable mutual information terms; clean use of information bottleneck principle
Impressive empirical results: up to 757× computational speedup on Tiny ImageNet with maintained or improved utility (e.g., 73.4% vs 67.2% retain accuracy on CIFAR-100 vs Bad Teacher)
Comprehensive experimental evaluation across multiple benchmarks, architectures, and scenarios (class/random unlearning), with extensive baseline comparisons (10+ methods) and thorough ablations
Strong reproducibility: detailed pseudocode (Algorithms 1-2), complete hyperparameter tables for all baselines, reporting across 5 random seeds, promised code release
Thoughtful two-regime approach addressing both standard (retain data available) and zero-shot (forget-only) scenarios, with zero-shot variant being particularly novel
Excellent efficiency analysis including GPU memory profiling showing consistent memory savings (1.3-2.0 GB vs 5-10 GB for baselines)
Honest treatment of limitations with Appendix G demonstrating graceful degradation under Neural Collapse violations rather than catastrophic failure
weaknesses: Limited threat model: operates under black-box/API-access assumptions where raw representations still encode forget set information; vulnerable to white-box recovery attacks. Claim of 'unlearning' is weaker than actual information removal.

Heavy dependence on Neural Collapse hypothesis for zero-shot variant with non-uniform quality: NC4=0.9996 on CIFAR-10 but only 0.9355 on Tiny ImageNet. Graceful degradation shows retain accuracy drops 93.2%→71.5% under moderate proxy noise (Table 13).

Limited theoretical justification for approximations: Gaussian parameterization (Eqs. 3-4) justified only by 'standard practice'; identity covariance appears arbitrary; no analysis of Monte Carlo approximation quality or gap to true mutual information

No formal privacy guarantees: relies on RMIA as heuristic proxy rather than differential privacy or information-theoretic bounds. In unlearning context, formal guarantees are important for regulatory compliance.

Narrow evaluation scope: only image classification on CIFAR/ImageNet with CNNs; unclear how Neural Collapse assumption holds for vision transformers, LLMs, or other domains; no evaluation on modern pre-trained models

Insufficient analysis of forget set composition: only fixed sizes (1, 5, 10 classes or 10% random); missing evaluation on larger forget sets (50%, 90%), label-imbalanced subsets, or temporally correlated forget samples

Hyperparameter sensitivity requires careful tuning, especially for complex datasets: β = 10^{-3} default works but Figure 5 shows performance degrades sharply with β ∈ {10^{-2}, 10^{-1}}; limited guidance for practitioners on selection

Incomplete baseline comparisons: recent concept erasure methods (LEACE, kernelized rate-distortion) cited but not empirically compared; UNSIR excluded from random unlearning; missing federated unlearning approaches

Permanent inference-time overhead (0.59-1.09 μs) accumulates at scale; justification assumes deployment scenarios with billions of inferences and that overhead remains constant under batching/optimization

Architectural choice under-motivated: why linear/shallow MLP sufficient for complex transformations? Section 4.5 shows stability but not mechanistic understanding of what features are preserved/removed
